lessons.title: Effective baselines and management of change — mechanisms
lessons.body:
Operations begins from a known required state, not from the last configuration somebody remembers. Maintain asset identity, hardware/firmware/software versions, controller projects, I/O mappings, network policy, identities, certificates, enabled services, backups, support state and dependencies. For each item, distinguish the approved baseline, staged candidate and effective running state. A repository commit proves a recorded change; it does not prove deployment. A running device can differ from both the repository and the last backup.

A change request must identify purpose, affected functions, dependencies, exposure, operating mode, expected benefit, test conditions, implementation authority, abort limits and restoration path. Routine security changes can affect physical operation through resource load, authentication, timing or communications. The owner must preserve the complete requirement set rather than treating the security ticket as an isolated task.

### Comparing state without confusing intent and execution
A baseline is a typed set of objects, not merely a directory of files. Model each object as (asset, interface, object type, approved value, effective value, observation time, provenance). Examples include firmware image, active boot slot, installed package, running service binary, application role, firewall rule order, PLC task assignment and retained force. A file hash works for immutable bytes; it does not compare the meaning of two configurations whose ordering or generated timestamps differ. Normalize only fields known to be irrelevant. Removing an entire authorization section to obtain a stable hash would hide the property being controlled.

Three comparisons answer different questions: approved versus effective finds unauthorized drift; candidate versus approved shows the intended change; recovery copy versus effective reveals whether restoration can reproduce the current service. None substitutes for the others. A useful drift report classifies differences as unauthorized authority, functional mapping, compatibility, operational data or harmless representation. Assign ownership and consequence before assigning urgency.

For example, a signed deployment package may install release 8.2 while a long-running service still executes 8.1. The package manifest and disk hash are accurate yet incomplete. Query the supported runtime version, process start time and loaded configuration, then exercise the changed behaviour. This is why acceptance evidence must observe the enforcing or executing instance, not only the administrative tool that prepared it.

worked_examples.title: Candidate configuration never published
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

Approved firewall candidateC18 denies engineering access from collectors. Running configuration remainsC17, which permits it; the change ticket contains only an editor screenshot.
worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: The approved candidate was never made effective on the device.
2. Translate it into consequence: The prohibited engineering path remains available despite administrative closure.
3. State the requirement: Acceptance must compare approved intent with effective deployed enforcement.
4. Implement the specific change: Publish the approved policy under change authority and verify the active revision.
5. Test observable behaviour: Attempt the prohibited path and the required collection flow on the running policy.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Alert on mismatch between approved and effective policy revisions; Reconcile candidate, running and recovery configurations after each change.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore the verified approved policy and correct the false closure record.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: An editor screenshot does not prove packet-handling behaviour.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: The change reviewer accepts observed effective state.

worked_examples.title: Standby becomes unavailable before patching
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

A patch plan assumed a ready standby host. Ten minutes before work, storage alarms place the standby in failed state; the active host remains healthy.
worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: A required availability prerequisite changed before execution.
2. Translate it into consequence: The planned patch can now remove the only functioning service instance.
3. State the requirement: Recheck operational prerequisites immediately before the change.
4. Implement the specific change: Hold the planned action and obtain a revised feasible operating decision.
5. Test observable behaviour: Demonstrate standby readiness or an approved alternative before proceeding.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Monitor prerequisite health throughout the maintenance window; Include live readiness checks in the execution checklist.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore the standby or maintain the active service under the approved deferral.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: The original change approval does not automatically cover the new degraded state.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: Operations and change authority decide whether revised risk is acceptable.

lessons.title: Effective baselines and management of change — implementation and evidence
lessons.body:
Use a state transition with explicit gates: proposed → technically reviewed → operationally authorized → staged and tested → implemented → verified → accepted or restored. Evidence should identify the actual target and release. Verify prerequisites immediately before action: standby readiness, current alarms, physical maintenance state, recovery material, staffing and access. A prerequisite that passed yesterday may be false today.

During implementation, record effective results and deviations. Do not bundle unrelated changes merely because access is available. If the change fails, use the pre-agreed stop or restoration path; first preserve relevant diagnostic evidence when safe. Afterward, compare the effective baseline, validate required service and prohibited authority, remove temporary privileges and update operational records. Closing a ticket is the final record of these actions, not the mechanism that performs them.

### A change is a guarded transaction
Treat a maintenance procedure as a transaction whose stages have preconditions and postconditions. Authorization grants permission for a stated scope under stated assumptions; it is not a guarantee that assumptions remain true. Before touching the active instance, evaluate a conjunction such as recovery_material_valid AND standby_healthy AND operational_mode_allowed AND staff_available. A false prerequisite causes a hold, an approved alternate path or an explicit emergency decision. It must not silently evaluate as true because a checkbox was completed earlier.

Record the exact order where intermediate states matter. Changing a controller certificate before installing the trust anchor at its consumer can break required communications. Updating both redundant peers before checking either can destroy the fallback. Conversely, an incompatible mixed-version cluster may prohibit an apparently safer rolling upgrade. The supported compatibility model determines the sequence.

Define abort thresholds with measurements and actions: a specified data-age limit, loss of a required independent path, unacceptable scan jitter or a failed protection interface test. An abort should identify the next safe action, not just say stop. Some migrations cannot be reversed in place; the fallback may be restoring a consistent snapshot plus reconciling transactions. Preserve diagnostic evidence when the operating envelope permits it. The change record should make the executed path and any deviations reconstructable.

worked_examples.title: Emergency rule survives ticket closure
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

An urgent repair adds a broad management rule. The incident closes, but no rule-expiry task or session-termination check exists.
worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: The emergency workflow omitted restoration of normal authority.
2. Translate it into consequence: Temporary broad access becomes persistent exposure.
3. State the requirement: Every exceptional permission needs scope, expiry and effective closure verification.
4. Implement the specific change: Remove the exception and terminate remaining unauthorized sessions under the approved procedure.
5. Test observable behaviour: Test new and established access against the restored normal policy.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Track emergency permissions beyond incident-ticket status; Reconcile exceptional rules and accounts during post-change review.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore the approved normal access boundary and assess the exposure interval.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: Deleting a rule may not immediately terminate existing stateful sessions.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: The incident and change owners jointly close emergency authority.

worked_examples.title: Rollback restores code but not schema
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

Application update migrates its database. Engineers reinstall the old executable, which cannot read the new schema, and call this rollback complete.
worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: The restoration plan did not treat application code and data format as a dependency set.
2. Translate it into consequence: The service remains unusable despite old software being present.
3. State the requirement: Recovery must restore a supported consistent code and data combination.
4. Implement the specific change: Use the tested compatible database and application restoration path.
5. Test observable behaviour: Run representative queries, ingestion and permissions on the restored combination.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Monitor schema version and application compatibility after change; Maintain paired recovery material and test migration reversibility.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore the approved consistent state and reconcile any data loss against objectives.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: An old installer alone cannot reverse an incompatible data migration.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: The application and data owners accept restoration consistency.

lessons.title: Effective baselines and management of change — independent lifecycle decisions
lessons.body:
For independent work, select a supported isolated system and create a genuine baseline comparison. Make one authorized change that affects an important requirement, prove it, then introduce a separate unapproved drift in the lab and identify it from evidence. Record differences at the right semantic level: a harmless timestamp change is different from a newly enabled management service.

Demonstrate one failed change and its recovery rather than presenting only a successful installation. Explain whether rollback restored code, configuration, identities and data consistently. Preserve any irreversible migration constraint. The acceptance reviewer should be able to reconstruct what changed, why it was permitted, what happened and which operational property was restored.

### Closure and exception debt
After execution, verify service, authority and recoverability as separate properties. Service tests cover required transactions and physical feedback. Authority tests prove forbidden operations remain forbidden, including established sessions and API paths. Recovery tests show the new baseline has usable restoration material. Closing only the service symptom can leave an emergency account, broad route or obsolete backup that creates the next incident.

Temporary exceptions need an identity, exact scope, compensating controls, expiry trigger and an accountable owner. An incident closure date is not a technical expiry mechanism. When the exception ends, remove the permission, terminate relevant sessions where supported, rotate exposed credentials and test both required and prohibited behaviour. If a legacy limitation prevents removal, change the record into an explicitly accepted residual risk with a review trigger; do not leave a supposedly expired exception operationally active.

Perform an independent reconciliation between the change record and observed state. The reviewer should be able to identify the target asset, old and new release, evidence times, test preconditions, defects, rollback status and residual uncertainty. Metrics such as change success rate require a definition of success that includes delayed defects and restored authority. Counting tickets that were closed by their authors measures workflow throughput, not sustained engineering correctness.

worked_examples.title: Hidden runtime override after approved project restore
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

The approved PLC project is restored, but a retained runtime force keeps one input true. The normal-state logic looks correct offline.
worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: Runtime forcing state is outside the compared source baseline.
2. Translate it into consequence: The restored sequence can act on a false permissive.
3. State the requirement: Recovery acceptance must include effective forces, overrides and physical inputs.
4. Implement the specific change: Remove the unauthorized force using the supported controlled procedure.
5. Test observable behaviour: Prove the real input and failed-permissive sequence after restoration.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Monitor active forces and unapproved runtime overrides; Review force state at maintenance handback and controller restart.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore normal input authority and recommission the affected sequence.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: Source-file equality does not establish effective runtime input state.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: The controls owner approves removal and recommissioning.

lessons.title: Network diagnosis from link to application — mechanisms
lessons.body:
Diagnose in layers while following one required transaction. Establish the physical link and error state, addressing and path, transport/session behaviour, application response, point meaning and physical outcome. Avoid treating these as a rigid checklist when evidence already localizes the problem: a valid protocol exception means some lower layers worked, while a single downstream serial unit failing behind a healthy gateway suggests a narrower fault than an enterprise outage.

Use baseline and delta evidence. Interface counters are cumulative unless explicitly reset; a large historical error count may not explain the current event. Record timestamps and calculate rates over a known interval. Correlate link errors, drops, queueing, CPU and application timeouts with load and maintenance events. A security incident and an ordinary fault can coexist, so do not force every symptom into one preferred explanation.

### Reading counters and traces causally
A counter is an integral over its observation lifetime. For a monotonic counter C, the rate over an interval is (C2 − C1)/(t2 − t1). Verify that both observations refer to the same interface and counter generation. A restart, reset, wrap or interface replacement can make subtraction invalid. Normalize units: packets, bytes and bits are different quantities. A short burst can cause a timeout while a five-minute utilization average remains low, so choose resolution that can expose the failure mechanism.

A trace establishes only what was visible at its capture point. A SPAN copy can drop traffic; offload can alter host-capture appearances; an absent packet may have taken another path. A capture on the client side showing a retransmission proves the sender did not receive the expected acknowledgment in time. It does not by itself identify where the original or acknowledgment was lost. Compare both sides of the suspected boundary using time uncertainty and transaction identifiers.

Distinguish transport sequence from application semantics. A completed TCP handshake establishes a transport session. A valid protocol exception establishes that a server understood enough of the request to reject it. A successful register read establishes a response for that address, not correctness of the engineering-unit mapping. Following a single business or control transaction across these layers prevents broad repairs based on an imprecise communications-failed message.

worked_examples.title: Large application records stall while ping works
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

Small pings and TCP handshake succeed. Large TLS records repeatedly retransmit after a tunnel change; path MTU signalling is not reaching the sender.
worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: The changed path cannot carry the application's effective packet size with working discovery.
2. Translate it into consequence: Application delivery fails despite basic reachability.
3. State the requirement: The path must support required application sizes and fragmentation or discovery behaviour.
4. Implement the specific change: Correct supported MTU and necessary control-message handling across the tunnel.
5. Test observable behaviour: Transfer representative application payloads and verify recovery without repeated stalls.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Monitor retransmissions and size-dependent failures after path changes; Retest MTU behaviour when encapsulation or security policy changes.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore the approved transport path and confirm current application data.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: Small ICMP success cannot establish large-payload delivery.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: Network engineering authorizes the path and MTU correction.

worked_examples.title: Historical CRC total mistaken for active fault
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

An interface shows10000 CRC errors, but its count has not increased for30 days. Current outages align with output queue drops rising during backups.
worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: A cumulative historical counter was mistaken for current error activity.
2. Translate it into consequence: Diagnosis can target the wrong physical component and delay service repair.
3. State the requirement: Use time-bounded counter deltas and correlate them with the symptom.
4. Implement the specific change: Measure current queueing and backup traffic before changing physical media.
5. Test observable behaviour: Repeat representative load and verify the actual loss mechanism is resolved.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Trend counter rates with synchronized event times; Retain baseline snapshots and clear counters only under documented procedure.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore required delivery by treating the active congestion cause.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: Historical error totals do not establish present signal integrity.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: The diagnosing engineer justifies intervention from current evidence.

lessons.title: Network diagnosis from link to application — implementation and evidence
lessons.body:
For a TCP application, distinguish no response to connection setup, explicit reset, successful connection with application denial, and a session that remains open while data becomes stale. A reset can be generated by an endpoint or an intermediary; packet position and surrounding records matter. Asymmetric routing can fail stateful enforcement, while MTU problems can let small tests succeed and larger transactions stall. Use controlled captures and supported diagnostics within the approved test scope.

For serial gateways, inspect downstream addressing, baud/parity/framing, termination and signal quality through appropriate safe methods. For redundant networks, identify which mechanism is actually deployed and what the endpoints expect. A route returning after failover is not proof that application state recovered. Measure the required transaction and freshness at the destination.

### Narrowing network fault domains
Start with the set of affected functions and the smallest shared dependency that could explain them. If one serial device fails while other units behind the same IP gateway respond, investigate unit address, downstream framing, bus state and device status before rebuilding the upstream firewall. If every consumer of one historian fails while controller-local loops remain healthy, separate supervisory loss from control failure. Fault scope is evidence, not proof: two independent faults can coexist.

A stateful firewall usually evaluates packet state as well as address and service policy. Return traffic on another unsynchronized member can be rejected even when routes exist in both directions. Policy counters, session tables and captures distinguish this from an application denial. Restore the intended supported routing/state design, then remove diagnostic exceptions and test failover. Leaving a broad bypass creates a second defect.

Packet-size failures deserve representative payloads. Encapsulation reduces usable path MTU. Small probes and session establishment can work while larger records stall if path discovery or fragmentation behaviour is broken. Test the actual application sizes under the approved configuration, not an arbitrary maximum ping alone. On a serial bus, changes in baud rate, parity, termination or topology can produce similar timeouts through different mechanisms; document the physical test authorization before intrusive electrical measurements.

lessons.title: Network diagnosis from link to application — independent lifecycle decisions
lessons.body:
The independent diagnosis must retain competing hypotheses and a discriminating test for each. Change one justified variable at a time where feasible, preserve before/after evidence and verify both service and security after correction. Do not fix a missing narrow flow by leaving an indefinite any-to-any rule.

Include a packet or event trace with supplied time assumptions, a configuration fragment and process evidence. Explain what each proves and does not prove. A protocol success confirms a particular operation's response, not necessarily actuator movement. Conclude with the effective corrected state and a regression test that would detect recurrence.

### A hypothesis ledger
Write a hypothesis as a causal claim and pair it with a discriminating observation. 'The network is slow' cannot guide a test. 'Backup traffic saturates the egress queue used by the supervisory stream during the 02:00 window' predicts rising queue drops, corresponding transaction delay and relief under an approved workload adjustment. A cable fault predicts physical error increments and may persist independent of backup volume. A denied application method predicts a valid server rejection with healthy transport.

Rank tests by information gained, operational risk and cost. Prefer existing counters and approved passive observations before disruptive changes. A negative result can be valuable only when the test had adequate coverage: no drops on the wrong interface does not weaken the congestion hypothesis. Record uncertainty, clock assumptions and sampling limitations.

After a justified correction, repeat the failing transaction and a security regression test. Reaching the server after an any-to-any rule is added does not demonstrate that the final narrow policy is correct. Capture the final effective configuration, required flow, denied flow and degraded-state behaviour. The incident record should retain the rejected hypotheses and why they were rejected so that future engineers do not repeat the same unsupported intervention.

lessons.title: Time, alarms, collection and detection engineering — mechanisms
lessons.body:
Operational monitoring is an engineered service. Define which events matter, where they originate, how they travel, how they are parsed, what time quality they retain, where they are stored and who acts. Include collection health and failure indication. A dashboard can remain green while its inputs stop, and a successful database write can preserve an incorrect timestamp or point identity.

Detection should correspond to a causal question: unauthorized project change, new management service, unexpected identity, prohibited write, loss of source freshness or failure of a required alarm route. Baselines need normal, maintenance and periodic modes. Correlate approved work and actual release identity rather than suppressing all activity during maintenance windows.

### Evidence time and event time
An event may carry device occurrence time, collector receipt time and indexing time. Preserve all three where available. Network delay and queueing separate them. Clock synchronization status is a further observation, not a reason to replace every timestamp with a single supposedly exact time. Represent an event time as an interval when uncertainty matters: if device A reports 10:00:00 with ±2 seconds and B reports 10:00:01 with ±2 seconds, their order is unresolved. A precise display does not remove uncertainty.

Retention is a capacity and policy problem. With event rate r, average encoded size s and retention duration T, raw capacity is r × s × T before indexing, replicas and margin. Use burst and outage assumptions, not only a mean rate. A forwarder queue that can hold 30 minutes does not guarantee continuity through a four-hour collector outage. Decide whether it drops oldest or newest records, whether it persists over restart and how gaps are signaled.

Collection coverage is end to end: source enabled, event generated, transported, parsed, stored, searchable and actionable. A green agent heartbeat proves only one link. A parser can silently discard a new firmware's event format while the transport remains healthy. Maintain a synthetic or approved benign test event with a known expected path, and distinguish test evidence from genuine production incidents.

worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: Monitoring lacks an independently evaluated freshness and collection-health path.
2. Translate it into consequence: Operators believe detection coverage continues during a blind interval.
3. State the requirement: Collection health must expire and alarm when expected updates stop.
4. Implement the specific change: Add bounded heartbeat age and storage/queue health detection.
5. Test observable behaviour: Fill the lab collector safely and verify failure indication and recovery of queued data.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Track event ingress, queue depth, dropped records and health age; Test capacity alarms and retention changes before deployment.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore storage and reconcile missing or delayed records with explicit gaps.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: The last green state is not evidence of current collection continuity.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: The monitoring owner accepts visibility only with tested health indication.

lessons.title: Time, alarms, collection and detection engineering — implementation and evidence
lessons.body:
Time correlation requires uncertainty. Preserve source time, receipt time, synchronization state and any known offset. Do not infer millisecond event order from clocks with seconds of unknown error. When normalizing, preserve raw records and document transformations. A trusted source can still be faulty; authentication and plausibility checks address different concerns.

A useful detection test includes a known stimulus, expected raw event, transport/parsing result, analytic decision, alert routing and response. Measure the required latency across that chain. Missing observations may reflect sensor placement, encrypted payload visibility, serial gateways, log permissions or collection overload. State these limits instead of interpreting no alert as proof of no action.

### Constructing a useful detection
Begin with the behaviour to detect and its required evidence. An unexpected project download requires identity, target, action, time and authorization context; a generic traffic spike is insufficient. A rule can correlate an engineering action outside its change window with a new source or unapproved account. Define what the rule cannot see, including encrypted payloads, local-console activity, unmonitored standby paths and devices without appropriate logging.

Tune suppression by mechanism. Deduplicate repeated notifications while retaining the original records and a count. Acknowledgment means a human has recognized an alarm; it does not prove the initiating condition cleared. Maintenance suppression needs scope and expiry, and critical conditions may require a separate route even during work. Global silencing prevents nuisance alerts and essential warnings alike.

Validate both sensitivity and false-positive behaviour. Feed a representative benign maintenance action, a permitted continuous operation and an unauthorized synthetic action. Check the context and destination of the resulting alert. The desired outcome is an actionable, timely decision, not merely a red dashboard tile. If collection fails, alert on that loss through a sufficiently independent path; otherwise a disabled sensor can make the site appear reassuringly quiet.

lessons.title: Time, alarms, collection and detection engineering — independent lifecycle decisions
lessons.body:
Build one detection from raw records and test it against an authorized event, an unauthorized event and a benign fault that looks similar. Record false positives, missed events, latency and the reason for each result. Tune the logic to preserve the security question rather than simply reducing alert count.

Operate the collection service itself: storage capacity, queue growth, dropped records, parser errors, time health, credentials, certificates and recovery. A SIEM is not an independent protective control merely because it aggregates logs; its usefulness depends on observable events, interpretable context and an effective response path.

### Detection operations and measurement
Separate data-quality incidents from security incidents while allowing escalation between them. Stale process values, missing heartbeats, excessive timestamp skew and parser failure can undermine the evidence used for security decisions. A zero-event period may mean inactivity or lost visibility. Correlate source health, transport health and expected baseline activity before concluding that the system is quiet.

Measure detection latency from the event occurrence to an actionable alert using stated clock assumptions. Measure acknowledgment and containment separately. A fast alert routed to an unstaffed mailbox does not provide rapid response. Percent coverage should use a defined population of required assets and behaviours, not every discovered IP address. An undocumented exclusion can make a high percentage meaningless.

Run periodic coverage checks after changes to firmware, topology, logging policy, certificate trust, collectors and role assignments. Retention tests should retrieve a known event near the required age, with provenance and access restrictions intact. Exercises should include a collector outage and backlog recovery: deduplication, ordering and timestamp handling matter when delayed events arrive together. Record actual test outcomes, not an assertion that the logging feature was enabled.

lessons.title: Host protection and application execution control — mechanisms
lessons.body:
OT host security must preserve the specific application workload. Identify runtime services, drivers, databases, engineering tools, network connections, scheduled tasks, local accounts and recovery utilities. Application allowlisting, anti-malware, host firewalls and permissions constrain different mechanisms; none should be deployed as a generic score without functional acceptance.

Distinguish code integrity from process behaviour. A signed application can load an unsafe configuration or excessive credential. A trusted directory can be writable by an untrusted user. A security tool can correctly detect a suspicious file while its automatic response creates an operational problem. The engineer needs both the security interpretation and the process dependency.

### Protection mechanisms and their boundaries
Antimalware, application control and hardening interrupt different paths. Signature or behavioural detection may identify malicious execution; application control constrains which code may execute; least privilege limits what the executing identity can do. None makes an application immune to misuse of its legitimate functions. A permitted engineering tool with a highly privileged stolen account can still make an unauthorized controller change.

Application-control policy must account for executables, scripts, libraries, child processes and approved update mechanisms. A path rule in a directory writable by ordinary users gives those users an indirect execution permission. A signer rule trusts a publisher within its scope; it does not identify one tested version. A hash rule is precise for bytes but changes when approved software changes. Select and combine mechanisms according to the supported platform and operational need.

Assess resource effects. Scanning a large historian archive can contend for disk access; inspecting real-time working files may be unsupported; blocking an unexpected helper process can interrupt a permitted failover. These are reasons for representative compatibility tests and narrow documented exclusions, not blanket disabling of protection. Retain ownership and review triggers for every exclusion.

Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

Allowlisting permits executables underC:\ControlTools. The operator role can create files in that directory and launch them.

1. Establish the mechanism: The path trust rule relies on a directory whose write authority is too broad.
2. Translate it into consequence: An ordinary account can introduce executable content into a trusted location.
3. State the requirement: Protect the policy's trust assumptions as well as its visible rule.
4. Implement the specific change: Restrict directory writes and use supported appropriate executable identity controls.
5. Test observable behaviour: Attempt an unapproved executable from the formerly writable path and verify denial.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Monitor directory permissions and executable creation in trusted locations; Review trust-path permissions after software installers and role changes.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore the approved directory and execution policy baseline.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: A configured allowlist is not effective if its trust source is attacker-writable.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: Host security and application owners approve required installation authority.

2. Translate it into consequence: Protection can prevent timely restoration during an outage.
3. State the requirement: Include controlled recovery tools in functional policy acceptance.
4. Implement the specific change: Add a narrowly justified rule for the verified supported recovery utility.
5. Test observable behaviour: Complete an isolated restore with the intended execution policy enforced.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Track blocked executions associated with approved maintenance and recovery; Retest policy after recovery-tool updates.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore the approved policy and complete verified database recovery.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: Disabling all execution control avoids rather than resolves the policy requirement.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: The recovery and security owners approve the narrow rule.

lessons.title: Host protection and application execution control — implementation and evidence
lessons.body:
Create a staged policy from required executables and workflows, then challenge it. Test normal acquisition, alarming, engineering work, scheduled maintenance and recovery. Record how policy decisions are made: path, publisher, hash or another supported attribute. A path-based rule relies on the directory's write permissions. A broad publisher rule may allow more tools than intended. A hash rule may need controlled updates when binaries change.

For anti-malware, define supported scan and response settings, update method, resource limits, exclusions and operational coordination. Test signature and policy updates as well as engine versions. Monitor CPU, storage latency, service restarts and quarantine events alongside process telemetry. Exceptions need exact scope, justification, duration and verification at removal.

### Deploying and maintaining enforcement
Start in an approved observation or audit mode where the product supports it, capture representative normal, startup, maintenance, failover and recovery workflows, then construct the proposed policy. A week of steady-state traffic may miss a quarterly calibration tool or the recovery executable needed during an outage. Observation informs policy but must not automatically approve every observed executable; malicious or obsolete activity can also be present.

Before enforcement, test a benign prohibited executable or action in the isolated environment and a required maintenance workflow. Verify the effective endpoint policy version rather than only the management-console assignment. An offline endpoint may never receive the new rule. Check tamper protection, local exception authority, alert routing and the recovery procedure for an accidental block.

For removable media, use an authorized transfer process that records source, expected content, verification, scan outcome and destination. A clean scan is evidence about the scanner and its detection capability at that time, not a guarantee of harmlessness. Prefer authenticated release provenance and constrained execution alongside scanning. Maintain the transfer station itself, including its update path, logging and access control. Do not connect unknown media to an operational controller merely to discover its contents.

lessons.title: Host protection and application execution control — independent lifecycle decisions
lessons.body:
The independent task is to build and test a supported isolated host baseline with one constrained application workflow and one protected recovery workflow. Demonstrate an unauthorized executable being denied and a required tool remaining usable. Introduce a policy error that blocks a legitimate task, diagnose from raw records and correct it narrowly.

Retain evidence that the effective settings match the approved baseline. Do not solve every conflict by disabling protection. Conversely, do not accept a security configuration that makes required operation or restoration infeasible. Record any unsupported control and the approved compensating architecture rather than silently claiming benchmark compliance.

### Handling failures without permanent bypass
If protection blocks required operation, first establish which control acted and why. An application crash occurring after an agent update does not establish causation by chronology alone. Collect the block event, process tree, policy version, resource observations and relevant application evidence. Reproduce within a representative approved environment where possible. A temporary exception should be narrowly tied to the identified object or operation and should expire after the tested correction.

Restoring protection after an incident includes effective policy, engine health, update source trust and coverage checks. A console reporting installed is weaker than a local test confirming enforcement. Test an endpoint that was offline through the campaign, an alternate boot image and a recovery build; these paths often reintroduce old policy or broad exclusions.

Maintenance acceptance should demonstrate both that required work succeeds and that a representative prohibited action fails. Keep logs accessible to authorized responders and protect modification of policy itself. If the platform cannot support a desired control, document the boundary and implement feasible risk treatment elsewhere, such as a constrained management path and monitored maintenance workflow. Never describe an unsupported endpoint as protected simply because a neighbouring server runs a security agent.

lessons.title: Vulnerability and patch campaign operations — mechanisms
lessons.body:
Maintain a treatment queue tied to actual assets and functions. For each advisory, identify applicable version/component/configuration, exposure, consequence, available fix, supplier support and uncertainty. Prioritize the relevant scenario rather than sorting only by score. An unsupported device or recovery image can remain a material risk even when it is absent from an online scanner.

A patch campaign has dependency and authority gates. Obtain trusted material, establish the supported combination of firmware, drivers, applications and data formats, test representative function and recovery, and schedule within the approved operating state. Compare the risk of delay with the risk of the change and document bounded interim treatment.

### Applicability before priority
An advisory describes a vulnerable condition, affected versions and sometimes required configuration or access. Match it to the actual product, component, effective version and feature state. An asset inventory that lists only a suite name may conceal a vulnerable embedded library. Conversely, an advisory for a disabled optional service may have a different attack path from the same defect on an exposed service. Preserve the evidence and uncertainty in applicability decisions.

Priority combines credible exploitation and consequence with operational feasibility. Severity scores do not encode every site's process impact, independent safeguards, exposure path or maintenance constraints. Avoid the opposite error of treating isolation as proof of impossibility: service laptops, vendor access, removable media and local users can cross an apparently isolated boundary. A deferral needs an accountable residual-risk decision, compensating measures, monitoring and a review date or trigger.

Track the complete affected population, including spares, standby peers, golden images, recovery media and temporarily disconnected devices. A vulnerable image can reintroduce the defect during a future emergency. Distinguish identified, evaluated, tested, deployed, activated and verified states. A downloaded package and a successful installer exit do not demonstrate that the vulnerable runtime was replaced.

8. Keep this limitation explicit: Package-manager success is not proof of effective remediation.

lessons.body:
Use pilot evidence that represents the target workload and relevant failure modes. Confirm required restart or activation; package inventory alone may not show the running code. Repeat normal operation, prohibited authority, alarms, time, data quality and recovery checks affected by the change. Measure resource and application effects, not just successful installation.

A deferral must identify compensating controls and their effective-state tests. If a temporary rule is removed, a new remote path appears or the device changes operating mode, reassess the acceptance basis. Keep spare devices and recovery images aligned so that the next replacement or restore does not undo remediation.

### Designing a patch campaign
Build a dependency graph covering operating system, drivers, firmware, engineering tools, database schemas, application versions and device protocols. Supported combinations constrain order. Test the exact package provenance and signature, prerequisites, installation, activation, required restart and functional regression. A test on a different driver or firmware family does not automatically cover the production combination.

Plan redundant systems from their actual compatibility rules. A rolling update may preserve service when mixed versions are supported; otherwise it can create inconsistent state or failover failure. After updating a standby, verify readiness and required replication before transferring service. Do not assume the presence of two hosts provides two independent recovery paths when both use the same storage or identity service.

A rollback package is a tested restoration method with known data effects. If a migration changes a schema, restore a consistent application/data pair or use the supported forward recovery. Define whether new transactions can be replayed and how duplicates are prevented. At each stage, evaluate health and abort conditions. Record deviations before accepting them, and leave the environment in a documented state if the maintenance window ends before completion.

lessons.body:
For independent assessment, process one applicable update, one non-applicable advisory and one deferred treatment with an explicit reason. Demonstrate a supported rollback or alternate restoration and preserve failures. Link every closure to running-state evidence and required function.

The operating campaign should show recurrence: a later advisory, a changed dependency or an expiring exception must trigger the right review. One successful patch is not evidence that the whole lifecycle process will remain effective without inventory, ownership and monitoring.

### Proving remediation remains effective
Verification must observe the relevant running component and, where feasible, the vulnerable condition's absence through supported safe checks. Do not run a destructive exploit against operational equipment to prove remediation. Use vendor-supported version/configuration evidence and authorized representative tests. The final decision should state which evidence supports the claim and which paths remain untested.

A campaign is not complete while the active peer is fixed but the standby, recovery image or spare remains vulnerable without an approved disposition. Reconcile all targets against the original scope and newly discovered assets. Handle exceptions individually, including unavailable devices, failed activation and unsupported releases. Retire superseded packages from normal recovery paths while preserving required forensic or records material under controlled access.

Evaluate post-change trends over a meaningful period: transaction errors, scan load, latency, alarms and security events. A short acceptance test can miss a daily batch or weekly failover process. Link delayed defects back to the campaign and preserve the ability to identify exactly which release was deployed where. Update restoration instructions and training so that the next recovery reproduces the verified baseline rather than the last familiar version.

lessons.title: Backup engineering and application-consistent restoration — mechanisms
lessons.body:
Backups are engineered recovery inputs. Identify the complete state needed to restore each function: firmware, configuration, projects, libraries, identities, keys, databases, historical data, licenses and supporting tools. Determine which parts must be mutually consistent. A crash-consistent disk image may not meet an application's recovery needs, and an old configuration can conflict with current authority or physical mapping.

Define RPO and RTO for the required service. RPO concerns how much data state may be lost; RTO concerns how long restoration may take. Neither is proven by a green backup job. Include retrieval, access, rebuilding, data restore, dependency recovery and acceptance tests in the measured restoration path.

### What a usable backup actually contains
A backup is a recovery input, not proof of recovery. Define the protected objects and their consistency boundary: controller project and libraries, recipes and retained values, application data and schema, certificates and trust stores, firewall configuration and required dependencies. Copying files while a database is writing can produce individually readable files that do not represent a valid application state. Use supported quiescing, snapshots or transaction-aware mechanisms and document their consistency guarantees.

RPO concerns tolerable loss of required state or data; RTO concerns time to restore the required service. A job interval is not an achieved RPO if recent jobs fail or the needed object is omitted. A fast image restore is not an achieved RTO if identity, licences, communications and recommissioning are still unavailable. Establish the start and end points of both measurements.

Separate confidentiality, integrity and availability of recovery material. Encryption protects confidentiality only while keys remain available to authorized recovery staff. A hash detects changes relative to a trusted reference; a hash stored beside a maliciously replaced image is weak provenance. Offline or immutable copies can reduce some modification paths, but their access, retention, key handling and actual retrieval still require testing.

lessons.title: Backup engineering and application-consistent restoration — implementation and evidence
lessons.body:
Protect backup integrity, confidentiality and availability with appropriate separation from production authority. If the same compromised administrator can encrypt production and delete every backup, the recovery boundary is weak. Preserve protected recovery credentials and verify that they work when production identity services are unavailable.

Test representative restores in isolation. Verify data consistency, application queries, current ingestion, authority, time and integrations. Reconcile revoked users and keys, obsolete rules and retired devices. A faithful restoration of historical state can be incorrect for today's approved system. Record the difference between restoring bytes and restoring trustworthy usable service.

### Consistency and dependency order
Draw a recovery dependency graph before an outage. A supervisory application may depend on name resolution, identity, time, storage, certificates and licences. Recovering the application before those services can create misleading symptoms or tempt broad bypasses. Identify cycles: if the password vault requires the directory service whose recovery credentials are inside that vault, provide an independently controlled bootstrap mechanism.

Do not blindly restore every backed-up security state. A snapshot may contain an account later revoked, an old trusted certificate, a vulnerable package or a temporary broad firewall rule. Reconcile recovery content against current authority and remediation records before reconnecting it to the operational environment. Recovery needs both a usable historical state and a current policy decision.

For data replay, preserve sequence, identity and idempotency assumptions. Repeating an already applied command can have a different effect from repeating a telemetry sample. Reconcile historian gaps without inventing measurements or silently relabeling interpolated values as observed. Document retained-value treatment in controllers: restoring setpoints and counters can be operationally necessary, but blind replay of a stale command or maintenance override can be unsafe.

lessons.body:
An independent exercise should include an unavailable directory or license dependency and one deliberately stale authorization item in the backup. Restore through the approved independent path, reject revived authority and demonstrate service under current requirements. Measure the complete sequence and state the exact environment.

Also test failure: unreadable media, missing key, inconsistent database state or insufficient restore capacity. A useful report explains what prevented the objective and what changed after correction. Keep physical controller and production acceptance separate from a local data restoration model.

### Restoration drills that establish evidence
A meaningful drill starts from an explicit failure scenario and unavailable components. If the drill assumes the normal domain controller, online licence server and administrator workstation are healthy, it does not prove recovery when those dependencies are lost. Choose scenarios from risk and service requirements, then record actual elapsed times, failed steps and manual interventions.

Validate the restored service with representative reads, writes where authorized, alarms, roles, communications and process feedback. Check forbidden actions as well as successful ones. Compare the restored effective baseline to the approved baseline and current revocations. For a controller, software restoration is followed by controlled verification of I/O mapping, forces, retained state, mode and sequence behaviour. Physical acceptance remains a separately authorized field activity.

Preserve honest results. If a drill misses its objective, record the measured result and the cause, improve the procedure and retest the affected dependency. Do not redefine the clock to start after the difficult part. A successful lab rebuild demonstrates the tested lab scenario; it does not prove production timing or physical behaviour. Maintain the distinction while using the drill to find defects before an actual outage.

lessons.title: Controller, instrumentation and supervisory maintenance — mechanisms
lessons.body:
Security maintenance must preserve the control application's physical meaning. Maintain approved projects, toolchains, I/O maps, instrument ranges, calibration records, override state, alarms, roles and startup behaviour. A controller can run approved code while receiving the wrong physical input or retaining a forced permissive. Conversely, a physically correct measurement can be hidden by stale supervisory delivery.

Separate software validation from physical commissioning. Simulation can test state logic and supplied faults. A real loop requires suitable safe equipment, calibrated references, wiring checks and qualified authority. Power-protection and switching decisions remain with their responsible specialists; BMS or EPMS integration does not transfer that authority.

### The effective controller is more than its project file
Control behaviour depends on source logic, compiled load, task scheduling, hardware configuration, I/O mapping, retained values, active forces, operating mode and field condition. Comparing project hashes answers only one part of the question. A controller with approved logic and a forced permissive can behave incorrectly; a correct input address with reversed engineering units can produce misleading values; a stale HMI cache can display a plausible number after acquisition fails.

Trace an analog measurement through sensor range, transmitter output, input configuration, raw count conversion, engineering units, quality and freshness. For a 4–20 mA transmitter, the nominal normalized fraction is (I − 4)/16, then engineering value = low + fraction × span. Out-of-range current, bad quality and stale timestamp are separate conditions. Do not clamp every failure into a plausible in-range value and thereby hide the diagnostic condition. Software scaling should be checked against an independent physical reference under an approved calibration procedure.

Digital signals also have semantics: normally open versus normally closed, de-energize-to-alarm, debounce, latching and reset conditions. A simulated bit toggle demonstrates a software path. It does not establish wiring polarity, contact failure behaviour or real actuator feedback.

lessons.title: Controller, instrumentation and supervisory maintenance — implementation and evidence
lessons.body:
For a supported logic change, compare the actual running project with the approved baseline, identify affected sequences and modes, test in a representative vendor environment, and plan the permitted transition. Include normal, maintenance, communications-loss, input-invalid and restart states. Evaluate timers, task behaviour, retained state and output initialization. Use the vendor's supported engineering and diagnostic tools rather than rebuilding its runtime.

After instrument or gateway maintenance, trace physical source to raw input, scaling, quality, timestamp, application point and control decision. Record as-found and as-left values and uncertainty. An authenticated gateway message does not prove correct range or physical placement. Restore overrides deliberately and verify normal command ownership.

### Sequence maintenance and control dynamics
Use an explicit state model for a pump or fan sequence: stopped, starting, running, stopping and fault. A start command is accepted only when current permissives and mode allow it. Starting must have a bounded feedback deadline; a command-success acknowledgment is not motor-running feedback. Loss of a required permissive during running must cause the specified transition. Reset clears a latched fault only under defined conditions; it should not automatically restart equipment unless the approved sequence explicitly requires it.

Restart semantics require deliberate design. Decide which state is retained, which is initialized and whether operator authorization is needed before resuming. Remove forces and maintenance bypasses through a controlled handback. Test cold start, warm restart and communication recovery because their retained-state behaviour can differ.

For a PID-controlled variable, preserve units, action direction, sample interval and output limits. Integral accumulation while an actuator is saturated can cause overshoot after the constraint clears; anti-windup is a design response. A sensor filter reduces noise while adding delay. Maintenance that changes sample time or network update timing can alter loop dynamics even if tuning constants are unchanged. Test changes within a representative model and then an authorized physical envelope; this course does not authorize live tuning by trial and error.

lessons.body:
The independent task is one complete maintenance cycle: identify a fault from evidence, obtain authority, preserve the baseline, implement a supported correction, test function and security, restore normal mode and update records. Include an actual safe physical measurement task where required by the curriculum; keep simulation-only claims bounded until that work is performed.

A handback should state current modes, alarms, forces, temporary rules, calibration, project identity, open risks and evidence location. Another operator must be able to understand what now controls the process and what remains limited.

### Integrated handback across BMS, EPMS and the field
A point-to-point test should establish source identity, address, units, scaling, status polarity, quality, freshness, alarm behaviour and destination meaning. Prove at least one independent physical reference for the relevant measurement class. A matching value on two dashboards may reflect a shared mapping defect. For EPMS, distinguish supervisory status and commands from independent protection functions; restoring a display must not be claimed as proving relay protection.

Cooling handback includes lead/lag selection, standby readiness, fail-to-start, low-flow or pressure conditions, leak responses and communication loss according to the approved design. Verify interactions rather than only isolated devices. A local controller may remain healthy while supervisory scheduling is unavailable; document which functions continue autonomously and which require intervention.

Record the actual versions of controller firmware, engineering project, function libraries, gateway mapping and supervisory application. Retain before/after evidence and the authorized test method. Close bypasses and forced points explicitly, with independent confirmation where required. The handback must name untested operating modes and physical limitations. A successful simulated sequence is a valuable engineering artifact, but it is not a substitute for vendor competence, calibrated instruments or site commissioning authority.

lessons.title: Incident triage, evidence and operational containment — mechanisms
lessons.body:
Incident work combines urgency with disciplined uncertainty. Establish the affected function, current physical state, observed authority changes, available safeguards and authorized response boundaries. Separate facts from hypotheses. A telemetry outage can reflect congestion, failed equipment or malicious action; an unauthorized project change is stronger security evidence but still needs scope and causal analysis.

Prioritize required physical operation while preserving evidence where feasible. A reboot, isolation or configuration correction can remove volatile context. Record the action, reason, authority, time and likely evidence effect. Do not let an investigation claim certainty that missing logs or unknown clock offsets cannot support.

### Triage separates observation, inference and decision
Begin with observable evidence: asset, event, time basis, affected function, current operating state and visibility gaps. Keep hypotheses distinct from facts. A new outbound connection can reflect compromise, a approved support action or an application change; an account name does not establish the human actor. Prioritize operational consequence and the possibility of further harm while preserving uncertainty.

Collect volatile information when it is relevant and safe before actions that destroy it. A reboot can remove memory evidence and terminate sessions; leaving a suspected host connected can permit further harm. There is no universal evidence-first or shutdown-first rule. The response authority weighs these effects against the process state and approved procedures. Record why the selected action was necessary.

Chain of custody records who collected an artifact, from what source, when, by what method, its integrity value, transfers and access. It supports traceability; it does not prove the source was truthful before collection. Preserve originals and work from controlled copies where feasible. A checksum mismatch may indicate changed content or a collection/transfer error; investigate rather than silently replacing the reference.

worked_examples.title: Controller download during authorized diagnostics
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

A vendor's work order permits reads only. Logs show a successful login and a project change, but the session recorder is incomplete.
worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: Valid access was followed by an action outside the documented task scope.
2. Translate it into consequence: Unauthorized logic may affect the physical sequence while attribution remains incomplete.
3. State the requirement: Bind support authority to permitted actions and preserve evidence of effective changes.
4. Implement the specific change: Contain the unnecessary download path and compare the running project with the approved release.
5. Test observable behaviour: Prove required diagnostics work while unapproved downloads are denied.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Correlate identity, target, release and work-order scope; Review support-session coverage and project-change permissions.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore approved logic and authority after scoped investigation.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: Temporal association does not conclusively establish malicious intent or sole causation.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: Incident leadership coordinates with controls authority on containment and restoration.

worked_examples.title: Automatic isolation removes only alarm gateway
worked_examples.scenario:
Synthetic engineering case; no live equipment was tested.

An endpoint response isolates the alarm gateway from all networks while local regulation remains healthy; no alternate notification path exists.
worked_examples.solution:
1. Establish the mechanism: Containment sacrificed a required operational-awareness dependency.
2. Translate it into consequence: The site may exceed its permitted unattended degraded interval.
3. State the requirement: Containment plans must preserve or replace required alarm coverage.
4. Implement the specific change: Invoke the approved alternate operational coverage and bounded containment plan.
5. Test observable behaviour: Exercise isolation with actual notification dependencies represented.
6. Preserve the corrected property: Track alarm delivery and degraded-mode duration during response; Rehearse containment with duty staff and updated dependencies.
7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore a trusted gateway and reconcile missed events.

lessons.title: Incident triage, evidence and operational containment — implementation and evidence
lessons.body:
Containment interrupts a path or effect; eradication removes persistence and cause; recovery restores trustworthy function. A revoked account can leave altered logic. A rebuilt host can inherit malicious policy from a compromised directory. An isolated gateway can remove the only alarm route. Model these dependencies before choosing actions.

Collect relevant host, network, controller, identity and process evidence under approved handling. Maintain source provenance, original records, hashes where appropriate and custody. Normalize time only with a documented basis and retain uncertainty. Coordinate qualified operations, controls, network, security, supplier and management roles without confusing advice with site operating authority.

### Containment is an engineering change under urgency
Select containment at the narrowest boundary that achieves the required risk reduction while preserving necessary control. Isolating an engineering workstation may stop unauthorized downloads without interrupting controller-local loops. Blocking a shared identity or time service may impair many healthy functions. Map dependencies and physical effects before broad isolation whenever the situation permits.

Credentials and sessions are different objects. Revoking an account can prevent new authentication while an existing session or token remains valid. A firewall rule change may not clear established state. Coordinate identity revocation, session termination, trust changes and network enforcement using supported mechanisms. Preserve emergency access through independently controlled procedures rather than leaving broad permanent access.

For suspected controller manipulation, inspect effective logic, forces, retained values and observed process behaviour using approved tooling. Do not assume that a malware scan of the engineering workstation proves controller trust. Containment may require supervised local operation or a defined fallback, subject to the process owner. Record the temporary operating envelope, staffing, time limits and escalation triggers.

lessons.title: Incident triage, evidence and operational containment — independent lifecycle decisions
lessons.body:
Run an incident exercise containing both a suspicious change and a plausible benign fault. Require competing hypotheses, discriminating evidence, a justified containment choice, continuity checks and explicit limits. Preserve the difference between a tabletop decision and a technical action actually performed.

After the exercise, identify one design or process weakness, implement a correction and retest it. The final report should explain what was known at each decision, what remained uncertain and why the chosen action met the operational constraints.

### Scope, eradication and controlled transition
An incident boundary expands or contracts as evidence arrives. Record searched assets, relevant time windows, indicators, techniques and visibility limitations. Failure to find an indicator on an unlogged path is not evidence of absence. Shared credentials, engineering projects, software distribution and recovery material can connect assets that do not normally communicate directly.

Eradication removes the identified persistence and exposure paths; it is not synonymous with deleting one detected file. Depending on evidence, use trusted reinstallation, credential rotation, corrected configuration, patched software and recovery-material review. Preserve the distinction between a host that runs normally and a host whose trust has been re-established. If the initial access mechanism remains unknown, state the uncertainty and choose additional controls and monitoring accordingly.

Before moving to recovery, verify that the intended restoration source and tools are outside the affected trust boundary or have been independently validated. Establish the acceptance tests and return-to-service authority. Maintain a decision log through shift changes. The final report should distinguish confirmed facts, supported inferences, unresolved questions and the operational decisions made under uncertainty. This creates reusable engineering knowledge without overstating attribution.

lessons.title: Trusted recovery across controller, network and platform compromise — mechanisms
lessons.body:
Trusted recovery must remove the authority and state that enabled compromise while restoring required service. Scope controller projects, network administration, host and BMC management, identities, keys, configurations and data. A reboot or successful boot is not a trust argument. A hash comparison needs a trustworthy reference, and an old clean image may still contain revoked authority.

Build the recovery dependency graph before an incident. Identify storage, network, time, identity, backup access, engineering tools, licenses and physical readiness. Avoid circular dependencies such as a backup console whose only login depends on the directory it must restore. Preserve an independently controlled recovery boundary appropriate to the scenario.

### Recovery restores authority as well as availability
Define the recovery goal as required function under an accepted trustworthy state. Rebuilding a host from a known image addresses executable state, but the restored application may still trust an attacker-controlled certificate or revive a revoked account. Reinstalling a controller project may retain forces or stale recipes. Recovering a switch configuration may reintroduce a temporary management path. Each layer needs a current authority reconciliation.

Separate three paths: network/platform restoration, controller/engineering restoration and supervisory/data restoration. They interact but have different evidence. Network recovery validates paths, segmentation, device identity and failover. Controller recovery validates compatible tooling, program/configuration provenance, runtime state and field behaviour. Supervisory recovery validates points, roles, alarms, historian continuity and mappings. A single image-restored checkpoint cannot cover all three.

Choose restoration order from dependencies and process requirements. Some local control can safely continue while the supervisory plane is rebuilt; other functions require coordinated shutdown or a defined manual mode. Document the approved operating envelope and the information available to operators during each stage. Recovery priority follows essential function and consequence, not the order in which servers appear in an inventory.

7. Restore function and trust if necessary: Restore platform authority before reconnecting the rebuilt host.
8. Keep this limitation explicit: A clean OS scan does not establish BMC integrity.
9. Preserve the authority boundary: Hardware and security recovery authorities accept platform trust.

lessons.body:
Use isolated restoration where feasible. Establish supported firmware and platform trust, restore approved application and configuration state, reconcile current identities and keys, validate required functions, then reconnect in a controlled sequence. Recommission point mappings, startup, alarms, denied actions and physical feedback. For a BMC compromise, OS reimaging alone does not address the management plane beneath it.

Define acceptance against the actual incident path. Controller compromise needs approved logic and process proof. Network-administrator compromise needs effective policy and removed management authority. Server/BMC compromise needs platform trust and management-path verification. Shared data and identity dependencies may require coordinated recovery across several domains.

### Reconciliation before reconnection
Build a reconciliation set from current approved configuration, revocations, vulnerability treatments, certificates, supplier access and operational changes since the backup. For each restored object, decide whether to retain, replace, revoke or quarantine it. A backup older than a legitimate setpoint change may require controlled application of that change; an old vendor account should not return merely because it was present in a valid historical snapshot.

Re-establish trust in recovery tools and communication channels. An image signed by a compromised signing key is not independently trustworthy. A certificate chain can be cryptographically valid while the endpoint identity or role is wrong. Validate provenance, applicable validity/revocation information and intended identity through the approved process. Preserve independently controlled bootstrap access for dependency outages.

Reconnect in stages with explicit hold points. Verify local service, then required dependencies, then boundary traffic and representative transactions. Observe prohibited authority and unexpected communications. Increasing access to make a restored application work can defeat the containment achieved earlier; diagnose the missing dependency and authorize the minimum required correction. Record each accepted stage and the conditions that would trigger isolation again.

lessons.body:
The independent assessment must cover three separate paths across the programme: control/logic compromise, network-authority compromise and server/BMC-management compromise. Use supported safe environments and state fidelity limits. Measure recovery time and data loss against declared objectives, including validation.

Prove both restored service and denied old authority. Keep unresolved firmware, missing evidence or untested physical behaviour visible. The acceptance authority decides whether remaining risk is suitable for service return; the tool's successful exit code does not make that decision.

### Return-to-service evidence and learning
Acceptance combines functional, security and operational evidence. Function includes representative modes, timing, alarms and physical feedback. Security includes corrected exposure, current identities, effective enforcement and detection coverage. Operations includes staffing, procedures, maintenance records, recovery material and unresolved risk ownership. A single successful login or green status page is insufficient.

Measure restoration from the declared failure point to the declared required-service criterion. Report partial service and full service separately. If data is missing, quantify the known gap, identify uncertainty and preserve quality markings. Backfilled or estimated values must remain distinguishable from observed measurements. A controller returning to run mode is not evidence that its physical sequence is acceptable.

After acceptance, use a defined heightened-observation period tied to likely recurrence and delayed effects, then transition to normal ownership. Close temporary accounts and routes, update the baseline and test that future recovery material contains the corrected state. Review how the incident was detected, where assumptions failed and which controls could have reduced consequence. Assign specific improvements with evidence of completion rather than declaring lessons learned solely because a meeting occurred.

lessons.title: Audit, service ownership and continuing improvement — mechanisms
lessons.body:
A sustaining programme must demonstrate recurring operation, not only project completion. Maintain vulnerability treatment, access review, configuration drift checks, backup restoration, supplier lifecycle, media handling, logging health, incident exercises and decommissioning. Link these to actual functions and owners so that a missed task has an operational consequence and escalation path.

Audit evidence should connect requirements to effective state and observed results. A policy, ticket or dashboard is one evidence source with limits. Distinguish completed activity from demonstrated control effect. Review exceptions at expiry and material change, and keep unsupported claims or untested gates visible.

### An audit follows claims to evidence
Start from a specific claim: only authorized engineering identities can change controller logic, required telemetry survives the stated failover, or recovery meets a defined time and data objective. Trace it to a requirement, implementation and observed test. A policy document describes intent; an installed tool describes a mechanism; neither alone demonstrates effectiveness. Use independent samples selected to expose meaningful failure paths, including exceptions and degraded states.

Define the population before measuring compliance. Ninety patched hosts out of one hundred known hosts is different from ninety out of an unknown estate. Include disconnected assets, spares and recovery images when they fall within the requirement. Record exclusions with reasons and owners. Avoid averaging away a high-consequence exception by reporting only the overall percentage.

Evidence ages. A site acceptance result predating a major routing, firmware or role change may no longer support the current claim. Link changes to affected requirements and determine the necessary regression scope. Do not automatically rerun every test, but do not assume an unchanged project filename means the relevant property is unchanged.
