lessons.title: Audit, service ownership and continuing improvement — implementation and evidence
lessons.body:
Use operational findings to improve design. Repeated broad troubleshooting exceptions may reveal that the approved maintenance path is unusable. Recurrent stale telemetry may require better source-quality handling rather than more server capacity. Repeated restoration failure may reveal a missing license or identity dependency. Measure the relevant outcome before and after a controlled change.

Automation can help compare configurations and evidence, but its authority needs limits. Protect inputs, dependencies, secrets and execution rights. Read-only AI or MCP diagnostics must treat retrieved text as data rather than instructions. A useful explanation does not authorize a tool to change controller state. Review the actual permission boundary and test hostile or stale inputs.

### Sustaining competence, suppliers and service ownership
Assign ownership to services and outcomes as well as components. A network team can demonstrate packet delivery while the application team still has a stale-data failure; someone must own the end-to-end function. Supplier access, update provenance, vulnerability notifications, support deadlines and recovery dependencies require continuing management across the contract lifecycle.

Train operators on degraded modes, alarm interpretation, emergency access, evidence preservation and handback. Knowledge quizzes establish recall and reasoning under the assessed conditions. Vendor-tool exercises establish the tested implementation skill. Calibrated field tests and authorized operations establish additional evidence. Maintain these distinctions in the competence record so that a certificate is not treated as proof of every site-specific capability.

For AI-assisted diagnostics, define the permitted data, advice and action boundaries. A read-only evidence helper should not possess credentials or tool paths that can modify plant state. Review its interpretation against primary records, preserve provenance and require authorized engineering decisions for changes. A useful diagnostic explanation does not establish that a proposed live action is safe or correct.

9. Preserve the authority boundary: Maintenance and security owners approve the redesigned workflow.

lessons.title: Audit, service ownership and continuing improvement — independent lifecycle decisions
lessons.body:
For the operating campaign, retain a sequence of dated tasks across ordinary service, maintenance, a failed change, diagnosis, incident coordination, restoration and improvement. Use actual results and identify the environment. One simulation cannot be relabeled as field experience.

At retirement, remove data and authority as well as the hardware item. Revoke accounts and certificates, sanitize according to appropriate supported guidance, update inventories and remove stale monitoring or trust relationships. Keep D1 building engineering outside the programme; later power/cooling engineering has separate specialist and physical evidence gates.

### Improvement as a controlled lifecycle change
Prioritize improvements using consequence, recurrence, exposure and feasibility. A repeated backup failure with no tested alternate path may deserve more attention than a large count of harmless alerts. Convert findings into verifiable outcomes: recover a representative service from independently available material within the objective; demonstrate expiry of emergency authority; detect loss of logging within a defined interval.

Retirement is part of maintenance. Remove device identities, certificates, routes, firewall rules, accounts, monitoring expectations, licences and asset records through a coordinated process. Preserve required records and evidence, sanitize media using an approved method and verify that replaced hardware cannot regain authority through an old credential. Simply unplugging a host leaves many logical dependencies intact.

Review improvement effectiveness after implementation. A new procedure that operators cannot execute during a dependency outage is incomplete. Use exercises and actual operational evidence to refine it, with explicit limits on what was tested. Preserve a portfolio of requirement-to-evidence chains covering design, implementation, commissioning, routine operation, maintenance, diagnosis, response and recovery. This supports the intended full-lifecycle engineering identity while remaining honest about external training, licensed standards and physical competence gates.

9. Preserve the authority boundary: The assurance reviewer approves improvement claims within their evidence scope.
